title: Answer to Question: The PKK and the Struggle between the Turkish Army and the Government
text:
Answer to Question

The PKK and the Struggle between the Turkish Army and the Government

Question: We know that the Turkish army and the Turkish government are at opposite extremes, so how did they agree on the decision of a military attack on the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) in Iraq? Bearing in mind that this attack will raise the stock of the army at a time when it creates embarrassment for the Turkish government before America, which occupies Iraq and especially Kurdistan, in view of the distinguished relationship between the Turkish government and the United States? Then why did Congress (the Senate) pass the law on the Armenian genocide at this time, which increased the embarrassment for Erdogan's government?

Answer: In order for the answer to be clear, it is necessary to know the reality of the Kurdistan Workers' Party, the Turkish army, and the current Turkish government.

As for the Kurdistan Workers' Party and its role with the army and the government:

The party was founded in 1979, but it actually came to prominence at the direction of America in 1984, in the era of Özal (1983 - 1993), when it carried out its first operations against the army in Siirt (a Kurdish city in the east of Turkey). It was intended by this to put pressure on the army in terms of security, simultaneously with Özal's pressure on the army militarily by establishing (a police force strongly and heavily armed), which continued in Özal's era until the end of his era; after his era the army confiscated the heavy weapons belonging to the security agencies.

The situation of the Workers' Party continued in this manner, as a security weapon in the hand of America in the face of the Turkish army, until the series of events between 1997 and 1998: the February 1997 movement, the government of Ecevit, England's veteran man, in June 1997, and his serious threat to Syria because of its support for the Workers' Party in 1998. Finally, America saw that its interest required that it conclude a deal with the Turkish army by way of the new Turkish government, since the political and military authority in Turkey had become of one kind, by abandoning the Kurdistan Workers' Party as a (military) organisation and ending the crisis with Syria, in order to preserve America's influence in Syria from being shaken. And so it was, as this was reflected on Syria, and calming talks took place between Turkey and Syria, which were crowned with the conclusion of the Adana Agreement in October 1998. According to the agreement, Syria accepted to stop its support for the Kurdistan Workers' Party, to expel Abdullah Öcalan, and to hand over a number of the other leaders in Syria to Turkey.

Öcalan left Syria for Russia, which refused him asylum, so he left it for Greece, then Italy, then he ended up settling in Kenya, where a unit of the special forces of the Turkish army went to Kenya and took delivery of him, by arrangement of American intelligence.

After that, America became active in Turkey through political, popular and democratic work ... until it succeeded in bringing Erdogan and his party to power in 2002.

As for the Kurdistan Workers' Party, it split: one section proceeded according to the new American approach to work, that is, to political work, under the leadership of Osman Öcalan, and one section was taken over by the English, and the influence of the Jews is clear in its course, its training and its leaders. This section came under the wing of the Turkish army, which exploits it in creating unrest against Erdogan's government, which is loyal to America, and at the same time to create a justification for the army to impose its presence whenever necessary on the pretext of eliminating the unrest. Thus, the American policy with regard to the Workers' Party, especially in the era of the Justice Party's government, is that the Kurdish issue be a political issue; while the English policy with regard to the Workers' Party, especially in the era of the Justice Party's government, is that the Kurdish issue be a security issue, that is, the opposite of what the situation was before the Adana Agreement. This explains the armed actions which the Kurdistan Workers' Party, the English wing, is launching at the present time.

As for the Turkish army, it is the creation of Mustafa Kemal, who, ever since he carried out the plans of the English by destroying the Khilafah, set about forming the army, in terms of its leaderships and its culture, upon loyalty to the English and their policy, and upon war against Islam in its thoughts and even in its sentiments. He used all brutal methods in purging its elements on whom he saw any signs of respect for Islam. He was not content with a member of the army not respecting Islam in order for him to remain and obtain promotion; rather, he even took into account the respect of the women of those members and their relatives for Islam.

Thus the army grew up upon secularism and upon loyalty to the English and their policies, and it considered itself the protector of the foundations of the republic which Mustafa Kemal laid down, based on the two previous basic lines: secularism and fighting Islam, and loyalty to the English. And the army considered itself a faithful guardian of these two crimes!

America tried earnestly to penetrate Turkey by infiltrating the army, which it sees as the effective force holding the reins of the country, but it could not, for it is saturated with the (English) approach of Mustafa Kemal. Each time, it would collide with the army's coup against the government if America's agents crossed not the red lines, but even if they crossed the yellow lines or approached them! Thus the army carried out the coups of 1960, 1971, 1980 and 1997, and their pretext each time was preserving the English secular system.

As for the current Turkish government, America has a long hand in its establishment and support, and that since it was able to have an influential weight in the Justice and Development Party, whose leadership was assumed by America's two men, Erdogan and Abdullah Gül, since its founding in August 2001.

After that, the preparation of the stage for Erdogan's arrival began. America withdrew (5-7) billion dollars from the Turkish Central Bank in 2001, since the economic privileges whose foundations were laid in the period of Özal enabled America to carry out this operation with ease and simplicity. It thereby created an economic shock, and the people's discontent began because the purchasing power of the lira fell very sharply, and the people's resentment against Ecevit and his government increased.

In the meantime, America was able to penetrate a small party that was in coalition with Yılmaz's party and Ecevit's party, namely the Nationalist Movement Party headed by Devlet Bahçeli, and it instructed it to request the holding of early elections and to threaten to resign if the elections did not take place. Thus early elections were announced on 3/11/2002, in which the Justice and Development Party won the elections by a landslide, especially as in its election propaganda it mixed secularism with a little of an Islamic tinge; yet, small as it was, it attracted to it the votes of the general Muslims because of the provocative hostility to Islam they had met from the secularists of the army and the Kemalists. Thus it won and secured the parliamentary majority, and formed the government alone.

Erdogan began implementing the drawn-up plan of strengthening ties with America and weakening the influence of the English, especially the army. Among the first of his actions was that he presented to parliament a law reducing the authority of the National Security Council to interfere in government, and likewise made the council mixed of military and civilian members. The army was irritated by this, to the extent that some reports leaked that the Istanbul bombings at the end of 2003 CE had (the military) behind them, in order to create a security disturbance which they could exploit to intervene, like the earlier February movement, but they did not succeed in that. In recent years, Erdogan's government proceeded to sign the Shared Vision document between the Turkish government and the government of the United States, which Abdullah Gül signed with Rice on 05/07/2006. Its broad lines, as they appeared in the press statement published on 05/07/2006 on the official website of the American State Department, began with an introduction which said: "We share common values and ideals in our regional and global objectives: the promotion of peace, democracy, freedom and prosperity."

Now, after grasping this reality of the Workers' Party, the army and the current government, the ongoing events can be understood. They are not unprecedented events, for the army has become accustomed to them after it lost the possibility of changing governments not to its liking through coups. The weakness of the army's ability to carry out coups has made it resort to blowing up the situation in terms of security in order to destabilise Erdogan's government so that it resigns or is dismissed, especially when it ventures upon what the army considers red lines.

Before taking up the recent events with analysis, we recall two important matters:

The first is the reality of the current chief of staff of the Turkish army, Yaşar Büyükanıt:

Büyükanıt is one of the men of the English in the army; indeed, he is one of the hawks on whom the secularists of the English pin broad hopes for returning the army to its strength and dominance. The General Staff hastened his appointment before the end of the meeting of the Military Shura Council on 4/8/2006, as is customary in such cases, so the Shura Council issued the decision on 1/8/2006. That is because the decision to appoint General Büyükanıt required sending it to the Prime Ministry for ratification following the holding of the meeting of the Supreme Military Shura Council (YAŞ) on 04 August 2006; but the generals' haste in that was the result of their fear of Erdogan organising a counter-campaign at the last moment.

The generals feared that Erdogan would prolong his foreign visits on the pretext of the Lebanese crisis, which would obstruct the holding of the meeting of the council of ministers, in addition to most of the ministers being outside Ankara and parliament being in its annual recess, and all this would lead to procrastination and the postponement of the ratification of the decision to appoint General Büyükanıt. Erdogan, who left Turkey on 02 August to attend the meeting of the Islamic Conference in Malaysia, intended to continue his foreign visits in order to delay the ratification of the decision to appoint General Büyükanıt. However, the generals, who realised that, forced Erdogan to ratify the decision before beginning his foreign tour, that is, on 1/8/2006, and before the Military Shura Council issued its decisions on 4/8/2006!

The secular circles in Turkey were waiting for Büyükanıt's arrival at the head of the General Staff with burning impatience. Therefore, it is expected that the period of his presidency of the General Staff, amounting to two years until August 2008, will be a difficult period for Erdogan, and it may lead to the stumbling of the course of the Justice and Development Party's government, according to the strength of the expected struggle.

It should be known that this general is intensely hostile to Islam like others, indeed he is more intense. He began his era by expelling (discharging) seventeen ranks of the Turkish armed forces because they had some Islamic sentiments, considering that, as stated in the reasons for their discharge, (their unsuitability for the army).

The second: The Justice Party's government is serious about reducing the authority of the army through parliamentary laws and democratic methods ... in keeping with the American policy, because the army is the mainstay of the English in Turkey, and limiting their authority and making the authority actually belong to the government, all this weakens the influence of the English and strengthens the influence of America.

The government has actually proceeded on this path, as it did in the National Security Council in 2003, when it made the secretary of the National Council a civilian after he had been from the army, and thereby weakened the authority of the army in the council. Likewise it did in the Constitutional Court, reducing the number of those loyal to the army in the court ... Thus the Justice Party's government is pressing ahead with reducing the authority of the army by way of enacting laws through democratic methods ...

After that, we answer what came in the question about the recent events and the decision relating to the Armenians.

18 Shawwal 1428 AH

29/10/2007 CE
